# PR #259: final round-2 correctness review

Head: 65d00078ba93664b1854d768d8531dcd0e2542f4
Base: 9543d9ada76614b59ffd06507d46c68497cbd4b8
Verdict: PASS

R259-001 and R259-002 are closed. No new normal-use blocking bug found in the PR delta. This completes the final C34 review round.

## R259-001: ordering and framing are now correct

The callback spy writes its called fact synchronously before invoking the real handler. For hooks, the installed SDK awaits its hook handler before answering hooks.invoke. For tools, it awaits the real handler before sending session.tools.handlePendingToolCall. Thus receiving the corresponding answer establishes that the callback's fact was already written, even though it may not yet have arrived on stderr.

After that answer, the parent sends a uniquely identified contract.barrier session event. The shim's already-installed SDK listener writes the barrier fact through the same say function and stderr stream as the callback facts. Waiting for this line therefore establishes that the earlier callback facts have arrived. The SDK's session event dispatch invokes the registered listeners, and nothing in the barrier path can move its write ahead of a callback write that preceded the earlier RPC answer.

The joined fact is written after the barrier listener is installed; the parent waits for it before issuing hook/tool probes. awaitFact also checks already-received facts, so a fast barrier response is not lost. readline now supplies complete records across chunk boundaries rather than parsing arbitrary chunks.

Verified against the installed 1.0.114-0 SDK's actual hook handler, tool handler and session-event dispatch implementations, and by running the supplied regression, not just inspecting its assertions.

## A missing callback still fails

A session-only Node loader changed the child extension's onUserPromptSubmitted property name to an unused name, leaving the SDK and repository files unchanged. The real canary returned:

- status fail, exit 1, elapsed 1 second;
- hook userPromptSubmitted: never reached;
- the other six checks passed.

The barrier therefore does not manufacture evidence or wait indefinitely for a missing callback. With no matching fact it reaches the negative assertion once stderr catches up. Transport/join/barrier waits remain bounded by the existing 10-second step deadline, with the existing bounded child shutdown afterward. The temporary loader was removed after the probe.

## R259-002: unknown reports no longer pass

The sensor now accepts only explicit pass, warn and skipped values. Missing status, unknown status, invalid JSON and nonobject output cannot fall through as pass; warnings retain the original output. A nonzero command exit remains fail regardless of its report body. The next-action guidance also correctly distinguishes SDK warnings from attribution warnings.

All seven real-adapter regression cases passed, including the three previously false-green shapes and the nonzero-exit override.

## Executed evidence

`just test harness/scripts/copilot-sdk-contract.test.ts harness/scripts/checks-copilot-sdk-sensor.test.ts` passed: 2 files, 8 tests. The real installed-SDK regression ran, not skipped, and passed all seven contract checks with every child-stderr event delayed 50 ms and data chunks split. This replays the round-1 ordering probe and adds fragmentation. The just recipe supplied nice 19; no outer nice was added.

The negative missing-callback canary used the recipe's own nice wrapper and returned the expected failure described above. No builds, cargo, general test suites, global configuration edits, pane mutations or version-record writes were performed.

CI run 44469430210 is successful at the exact reviewed head. Both Node jobs and Rust gates passed; the latest effective Delivers check passed. `just pr-freeze 259` returned FINAL twice, with matching full heads, main base, CLEAN and latest checks passing.

`git diff --check 9543d9ada76614b59ffd06507d46c68497cbd4b8...HEAD` passed. The review worktree remains tracked-file clean and target/ remains absent.

## Cost, isolation and harness feedback

The production delta adds no subprocess launch site. Barriers add three in-process stdio event exchanges per canary run; joined/fact waits and readline add no polling loop. The late/split-stderr preload is explicitly imported by the regression's parent process only, not propagated through NODE_OPTIONS into normal extension children. Its timers and extra canary/version launches belong to the on-demand test run, not the daemon or a per-seat background path.

The canary's child environment and private state/address isolation are unchanged. The shim handles the synthetic event only inside this isolated test session. No account names or machine home paths were added to the record or production sources.

magicWand resolved: callback evidence is now line-framed and synchronized through its own ordered channel, with an executable delayed/fractured-stream regression. The malformed-report lesson is likewise encoded in a focused real-adapter test.
